title: Ubisoft establishes Motherbrain subsidiary focused on AI gameplay, NPC memory and AI game masters
author: imlo2
selftext:
I was looking for news etc. about AI use in game dev/creative work in general, and noticed Ubisoft's latest investor reports, and came across something interesting.

In its November 19 earnings report, Ubisoft confirms that it has established Motherbrain, the team behind its earlier Teammates AI gameplay experiment, as a dedicated subsidiary. (*Teammates was in news already a year ago when they made the research project public.*)

According to Ubisoft, the focus includes:

* New forms of AI-driven gameplay
* Smart NPCs with memory
* AI game masters managing large-scale systemic worlds
* Developing technology for creators both inside and outside Ubisoft

It seems that this is more focused on AI as part of the actual gameplay rather than just generating assets or speeding up production, so it's not exactly annoucement of full-spectrum AI usage for everything (*But I would imagine they're going to leverage gen AI heavily for content, although nothing like that was mentioned unless I'm mistaken.*)

It's still an announcement of direction and not so much of a finished product, but I think it's interesting to see a major publisher making a dedicated organizational commitment to this area.

**Sources:**

[Ubisoft's official earnings report – November 19, 2026 (PDF)](https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/8aefmxkxpxwl/3zWBw9DLFyjmXNAGPYBi3F/a9bbd72b5f2ef790c254e4fd21cfcd04/Ubisoft_FY27_H1_Earnings_PR_EN_vF.pdf), page 4

[Ubisoft's earlier Teammates gameplay experiment](https://news.ubisoft.com/en-gb/article/3mWlITIuWuu0MoVuR6o8ps/ubisoft-reveals-teammates--an-ai-experiment-to-change-the-game)

comments.author: Gear-Usual
comments.body: North Side Inc has shipped Bot Colony Redux on October 30 2026 in Early Access and the game uses language as the main game mechanic (Ubisoft announcement), with NPCs that have memory, personality, can execute commands, are completely 3d scene aware - tech we’ve been working on and refining for 17 years. The game is playable in 16 languages and you can say anything - the characters will answer in context. Our game uses LLM, Speech-to-text and emotive Text-to-speech.

comments.author: VortexAssetStudio
comments.body: Makes total sense for a big publisher to focus R&D on systemic gameplay and NPC memory first, especially since they can afford the backend infrastructure for it. For smaller indie teams, keeping visual art direction cohesive and curated is still the main bottleneck, while runtime AI game masters are way harder to pull off without running into API cost issues

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body:
I think this is a good move, since the problem has traditionally been in any open world or AAA game with storytelling that the story content costs too much to create. And they are probably trying to solve that. Cyberpunk and many other games are great examples of how the world stops living (pretty much) the moment you complete the story. You're just after that just wandering around in an empty set.

Anyway, this would help with the issue for big AAA companies like Ubisoft, and could push games finally more towards open ended type of experiences, if people want that.

replies.author: VortexAssetStudio
replies.body: Yeah, that post-story empty world feeling in games like Cyberpunk is such a classic problem. Having NPCs actually react and remember things dynamically would give those big open worlds way more replayability once the scripted quests run out.
